<!--
A ticket for pybers, filed by a maintainer. `/ticket-create` writes the same shape and files it.

Title: at most about 60 characters, imperative and verb-first, sentence case, no trailing punctuation. It becomes the branch name, the pull request title and the CHANGELOG entry.

Label: exactly one of feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs or chore.

Sections: only those below, in this order, and no other. A measurement goes in `docs/findings/`, a settled decision in `docs/decisions.md`, and anything else in a comment on the ticket or in a ticket of its own.
-->

As a [role] I want [outcome] so that [reason].

## Acceptance criteria

<!--
Each criterion states an outcome someone can check, never how the code is built. Number every line `1.`, since Markdown counts them. One level of nesting at most, cited as `4.ii`. Cover user docs with examples, for `import pybers` and the CLI or TUI, and the developer docs the change adds to, corrects or removes, or name the ticket that does.
-->

1. [an outcome someone can check]
1. [another]
   1. [a nested outcome, cited as 2.i]

## Design

<!--
Optional, so delete this section when nothing belongs here. Design reference for a CLI, TUI or GUI: specifications, Figma links, screenshots or wireframes. Never implementation details, and never in place of an AC.
-->

- [a specification, a link or an image]

## Constraints

<!--
Optional, so delete this section when nothing belongs here. Two or three lines at most, each a fact already established that a competent build would otherwise get wrong without failing. Never a plan.
-->

- [a measured fact that rules out the obvious approach]
